name: T.J. Ricci
notes: Keeping this record. His middle name, Jeffrey, is for a cousin on his father's side.

name: Anna Marie Ricci
notes: Named for her great-grandmother on the Ricci side.

name: Jazlyn Morkert
notes: DeAnn's daughter, so T.J.'s half-sister on his mother's side. Named as one of Joe Morkert's nieces in 2003. Her father is not recorded here.

name: DeAnn Adel Morkert
notes: Her middle name, Adel, is for her grandmother Blanche Adele. She grew up around Scandia and Forest Lake.

name: Rodney Leo Morkert
notes: Named as a son in his father's 2011 obituary, and as the father on all three of his children's birth records. His middle name, Leo, is his father's.

name: Susan Marie (Houle) Morkert
notes: Born in 1949 and appears as a one year old in the 1950 census at Forest Lake Township. Named as a daughter-in-law in Orris Morkert's obituary.

name: Kenneth Leo Morkert
notes: Lives in the Scandia and Forest Lake area.

name: Rebecca Morkert
notes: Kenneth's wife.

name: Olivia Morkert
notes: Kenneth and Rebecca's daughter. She is one of the four nieces and nephews named in Joe Morkert's 2003 obituary, alongside T.J., Anna and Jazlyn.

name: Joseph Robert "Joe" Morkert
notes: DeAnn's younger brother. He died at 27, living in Fridley and formerly of Scandia. The funeral was at St. Peter's Catholic Church in Forest Lake.

name: Orris Leo "Porky" Morkert
notes: Born on a farm at Leeds in North Dakota and known all his life as Porky. He registered for the draft at Leeds in June 1942, and moved to Minnesota after the war, settling around Forest Lake. His obituary names four children: Katherine Swingle, Rodney, Paulette Paumen and Richard.

name: Evelyn Anetta (Gunderson) Morkert
notes: Born at Harlow in Benson County, twenty miles from Leeds, so she and Orris were both North Dakota farm children from the same county. Her Social Security file names her parents as Anton and Inga Gunderson, which puts a Norwegian line into a family that is otherwise German and French-Canadian. She is buried at Scandinavian Cemetery in Forest Lake.

name: Archibald Monroe "Archie" Morkert
notes: Born at Lafayette, Indiana on 4 April 1888, by his First World War draft card; a young single man in Alabama in 1910, and a farmer at Leeds in North Dakota from at least 1917 until 1950. He then went west: the Washington death index has him dying at Puyallup, Pierce County, on 12 December 1971. The open queue records a grave date of 1972, which has not been checked here, so the year of death is not fully settled. His son Donald Richard, born at Leeds in 1930, died in 1982.

name: Julia B. (Larson) Morkert
notes: Born in North Dakota, the first person on this branch not born east of the Mississippi. She was still at Leeds with Archibald in the 1950 census and died on 18 December 1958. Her maiden name is now on a record: her son Donald's Social Security file names his mother Julia B. Larson. The Find a Grave index puts her burial at Woodbine Cemetery in Jo Daviess County, Illinois; Archibald died at Puyallup, Washington, which has a Woodbine Cemetery, and this index has mislabelled cemeteries on this family before, so Puyallup is the likely answer. Her own parents are not yet known.

name: Henry Newton Morkert
notes: Born in Indiana in February 1851 and married to Mary Thompson in Carroll County on 22 January 1875, which the 1900 census confirms by recording twenty-five years married. The family did not go from Indiana to North Dakota and stay: all six known children were born in Indiana, the last about 1888; they were farming in Benson County, North Dakota by 1900; in Baldwin County, Alabama by 1910; living with their son Gust at Blackduck in Beltrami County, Minnesota in 1920; and back in Benson County by 1930. His 1880 and 1900 entries both give his own parents as born in Ohio, which is what points to Elias and Elizabeth, and the 1870 census puts him in their household at 19. His 1920 entry instead makes his mother a Pennsylvanian, which may be the enumerator reaching back a generation, since Elizabeth's own parents were born in Pennsylvania. His surname is written Merket in 1870, Market on the marriage licence, Markert in 1900 and 1920, and Morkert by 1930.

name: Elizabeth (Morkert) Hullman
notes: The eldest known child of Henry and Mary, born six months after their marriage. Her Social Security record names both parents and is where Mary's maiden name is written out. Her surname appears as Hullman and as Huffman, and she is very likely the daughter whose 1959 death record in Teton County, Montana already sits in these sources, though that has not been checked against her directly.

name: Mary M. (Thompson) Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio and with Henry in Indiana, North Dakota, Alabama, Minnesota and North Dakota again. Her maiden name is Thompson, from her own marriage licence of 22 January 1875 in Carroll County, Indiana. Two of her children's records say the same. The marriage licence is the one that settles it, because it does not depend on a child remembering. The censuses put her birth between 1856 and 1859.

name: Joseph C. Morkert
notes: Archie's older brother, two years old in the 1880 census. He went to North Dakota too, and earlier research has him prominent in Leeds.

name: Gustave L. Morkert
notes: Named as a son in the 1900 census at Beaver Township, born in Indiana. By 1920 he was a widower at Blackduck in Minnesota with six children and with his parents living in his household. His children were born in North Dakota, Alabama and Missouri, which traces the family's movements between 1906 and 1917.

name: Salamon D. Morkert
notes: Named as a son in the 1900 census at Beaver Township, Benson County, North Dakota, born in Indiana; the birth year is estimated from his age there.

name: Levi N. Morkert
notes: Named as a son in the 1900 census at Beaver Township, Benson County, North Dakota, born in Indiana; the birth year is estimated from his age there.

name: Elias Silas Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio and farming in Clay Township, Carroll County, Indiana. The 1870 census puts Henry, 19 and born in Indiana, inside this household rather than two doors away, alongside Elizabeth at 43 and four younger children, two of whom, Markas and George N., are the Marquis D. La and George W. who are still with Elias in 1880. That is what ties the two households together. The 1870 index gives Elias's age as 30, which cannot be right beside a wife of 43 and does not fit a birth in 1821; the original page has not been read to see whether the enumerator wrote 49. Henry's 1900 census entry gives both of his parents as born in Ohio, which is now the second census to say so and fits Elias and Elizabeth, though his 1920 entry makes his mother a Pennsylvanian. The link to Henry is still not stated by any document, because the 1870 census records no relationships, so it remains an inference, but a much closer one than before. Henry's 1933 North Dakota death record would settle it outright. A Jno L. Morkert heads a household at Gratis in Preble County, Ohio in the 1820 census, the year before Elias was born in Ohio, which is the likeliest place this family was living then.

name: Elizabeth (Burkhalter) Morkert
notes: Born in Ohio to parents born in Pennsylvania. The surname comes from FamilySearch's own linking of this census entry to an Indiana marriage record, so it is a lead rather than a reading of the register itself. Burkhalter is Swiss German. She appears at 43 in the 1870 household, which fits a birth about 1827 and corroborates the 1828 already recorded.

name: Lloyd Harry Houle
notes: He lived to 98 and spent nearly all of it in Forest Lake. He is buried at Calvary Cemetery there, although one index mis-maps the burial to a Calvary Cemetery in Washington County, Pennsylvania.

name: Blanche Adele (LaCasse) Houle
notes: Grew up in Centerville and married at Anoka in 1941. Her granddaughter DeAnn carries her middle name.

name: Cyril Joseph (Cyrille) LaCasse
notes: Head of a Lacasse household in Centerville in 1920 and 1930, written Cyrille in one census and Cyril in the other. His 1942 draft card gives Cyril Joseph, born 4 December 1888 at Centerville, living at Hugo. His death record names his parents as Tellsford, almost certainly Telesphore, LaCasse and Alphonsine Parenteau. He and Delina were killed together late on the night of 14 March 1964, when a Northern Pacific train struck their car at a crossing near Hugo that had no electric signals; the crossing is today's 140th Street, per T.J. The index of Blanche's 2007 obituary lists Walter, Clem, Eugene, Cyril and James Lacasse, Marie Tauer and Eva Kline among her relatives; they are most likely her brothers and sisters, but the index does not state the relationships.

name: Delina (LaMotte) LaCasse
notes: Named in the 1920 and 1930 censuses. Her death record proves the LaMotte maiden name that earlier research had without a document: her parents were John Lamotte and Rosalyn Tatreau. She died with Cyril in the car and train crash near Hugo on 14 March 1964; the Associated Press gave her age as 76 and printed her name as Celina.

name: John Joseph Houle

death.place: Forest Lake Township, Washington County, Minnesota

notes: He is the correction at the heart of this site. Earlier research had Lloyd's father as a David Houle born at Fort Ripley. The 1930 census and his own death record say otherwise: Lloyd was his son, and his own parents were John A. Houle and Mathilda Letourneau.

name: Lydia B. (Bernier) Houle
notes: She married at eighteen and appears with the family in the 1930 and 1940 censuses. Her death record names her parents as Joe Bernier and Emmile Forcier, and in 1910 she is at home in Centerville with them and four brothers and sisters. The state birth index gives 20 June 1896. She died at Forest Lake in 1982.

name: John A. Houle

death.place: Forest Lake Township, Washington County, Minnesota

notes: The first of this line born in America. The 1900 census narrows his birth to November 1868 and says he married in 1889; by 1910 he and Mathilda were at Columbus, a few miles from Centerville. He is six years old in the 1875 household with his father, mother and grandfather. His brothers there are Philias, Theodore, Thomas and William, and the eldest, Philias, was born in Michigan.

name: Mathilda (Letourneau) Houle
notes: Married John A. Houle in 1889 and appears with him and the children in the 1900 and 1910 censuses. Her surname comes from her son's death record. No birth year, no parents, and no record of her own has been found yet.

name: John Baptiste Houle
notes: His full name was John Baptiste, and his memorial gives an exact birth of 22 August 1842. He was brought from Quebec as a boy and died at Centerville eighty-six years later, buried at Saint Genevieve with his father. The 1900 census says he had been married thirty-three years, which puts the wedding at about 1867, and gives both of his own parents as born in French Canada. His Quebec baptism has been found: Jean-Baptiste, baptised 22 August 1842 at Saint-Aime in Massueville, Richelieu County, son of Michel Houle and Genevieve Cartier. The date matches his memorial exactly, and that match is what joins this family to the Quebec registers.

name: Virginia (Tourville) Houle
notes: Twenty-eight in 1875 and fifty-three in 1900, born in French Canada both times, so she came from Quebec rather than being born here. She and John Baptiste were married about 1867 and had at least eight children. A Euphemie Tourville, fourteen and also Quebec-born, is in the household in 1875, most likely her sister.

name: Michel "Michael" Houle
notes: He is at Centerville in the 1875 state census aged 70 and again in 1895 aged about 89, and his memorial gives 29 September 1802 to 6 December 1898, buried at Saint Genevieve Cemetery. One warning about the memorial: the index maps Saint Genevieve Cemetery to Shoreham, Vermont. It is Centerville, Minnesota; a Zotique Houle in the same Vermont-labelled cemetery and in the Minnesota county death register on the same day in 1897 gives the error away. Quebec now reaches him. He married Genevieve Cartier at Saint-Michel-d'Yamaska on 24 February 1829, a farmer and an adult son of Joseph Houle, farmer, and the late Jeanne Loiseau dite Cardin; his father and a brother, Jean Houle, stood as witnesses. Their son Jean-Baptiste, the John Baptiste of Centerville, was baptised at Saint-Aime in Massueville on 22 August 1842. Genevieve died in 1847, and in 1848 he married Marie Lataille at Sainte-Victoire-de-Sorel; Thomas was her son. Matching the Quebec man to the Centerville one rests on John Baptiste's exact birth date and Thomas's 1851 birth, so the Quebec part of his life is probable rather than record. His birth year is unsettled. The memorial says 1802. The censuses give ages that point to about 1805 or 1806, and a FamilySearch tree has him baptised at Yamaska on 30 September 1806, a day after the memorial's birthday; that baptism has not been opened here. Against 1806, the 1829 marriage calls him majeur, which under the law then meant twenty-five or over. Until the baptism is read, 1802 stands with that caveat.

name: Thomas Houle
notes: John B.'s younger half-brother, and the reason Michel could be named at all. His 1934 death record gives their father as Mitchell Houle and his own mother as Kadzi Tougon. His Quebec baptism, 21 September 1851 at Sainte-Victoire-de-Sorel, names his mother as Marie Lataille, Michel's second wife, so Kadzi Tougon is a clerk's rendering of her name and not a separate woman. The identification rests on the matching year, father and place of origin, so it is probable.

name: Anton Gunderson
notes: Named on his daughter's Social Security file. Born in Norway, 6 October 1888 by his memorial (the 1930 census says about 1889), and came to America in 1909. He farmed in Butte Valley Township, Benson County, north of Harlow, and is buried at Our Saviour Lutheran Church Cemetery there. His children with Inga included Gena (Gronvold), Evelyn, Agnes (Tufte), Nina (Berg), Alvin, Gilmen and Roy; Agnes's 2014 obituary names them. His Norwegian home parish is the next thing to find.

name: Inga Gunderson
notes: Named on her daughter's Social Security file. Born in Minnesota on 6 January 1898 by her memorial, buried at Our Saviour Lutheran, Harlow. Her maiden name is still unknown.

name: John L. Morkert
notes: Head of a household at Gratis, Preble County, Ohio in the 1820 census, the year before Elias Morkert was born in Ohio. An 1820 census names only the head, so this is a name and a place and nothing more. Earlier research named a John Lewis Morkert as an early American ancestor and put him in Indiana. The name turns out to be real and the place turns out to be Ohio. Whether he is Elias's father is not proven.

name: Dylan Morkert
notes: Kenneth and Rebecca's son. He is not among the four nieces and nephews listed in the 2003 obituary, so he was most likely born after it.

name: Geneviève Cartier
notes: Michel Houle's first wife and the mother of John Baptiste. She married Michel at Yamaska on 24 February 1829, still a minor, and was buried at Saint-Aime in Massueville on 6 June 1847, leaving him with young children; he remarried the next year. John Baptiste's 1842 baptism at Saint-Aime names his parents as Michel Houle and Genevieve Cartier and falls on the exact birth date his Minnesota memorial gives, which is what connects the Quebec family to the Centerville one. That connection is inference from matching dates and names, so she is probable rather than record. Her own parentage is stated twice, in her marriage and at her burial: Louis Cartier and Dorothee Ritchot. Her other children by Michel include Genevieve, Mathilde, Emilie-Philomene and Guillaume. A FamilySearch tree gives her a baptism of 25 July 1811 at Yamaska, which has not been checked here.

name: Marie Lataille
relation: second wife of Michel Houle, 5th great-grandfather
notes: Michel Houle's second wife, whom he married at Sainte-Victoire-de-Sorel after Genevieve Cartier died. She is Thomas Houle's mother: his baptism there on 21 September 1851 names his parents as Michel Houle and Marie Lataille. She was buried at Sorel on 24 April 1854, daughter of Louis Lataille and Judith St-Martin. Thomas's 1934 Minnesota death record calls his mother Kadzi Tougon, which earlier versions of this site took for a separate woman; it is almost certainly a clerk's hearing of her name, and a FamilySearch tree carries her as Marie Taillon Lataille. She is not T.J.'s ancestor; the direct line runs through Genevieve. Her sons Louis and Philias were also Michel's.

name: Joseph Houle
notes: Michel's father, named in Michel's 1829 marriage as Joseph Houle, farmer, and present at it as a witness, so he was alive in February 1829. His own marriage to Jeanne Loiseau at Sorel on 1 February 1796 writes him only as Joseph, of age, farmer, with no surname and no parents. That makes the Sorel act his only by inference: the bride's name is the one the 1829 act gives for Michel's mother. His parents are unknown, and this is where the Houle surname line stops. FamilySearch trees call him Joseph Petrin dit Houle, born 1767, and one contributor records a family story that he was raised by a farmer named Francois Petrain at Yamaska. None of that is sourced, and it is recorded here only as a lead. A son Jean Houle witnessed the 1829 marriage as Michel's brother.

name: Jeanne Loiseau dite Cardin
notes: Michel Houle's mother, dead by the time of his marriage in February 1829, where she is the late Jeanne Loiseau dite Cardin. She married Joseph at Sorel in 1796 with the consent of her father, Jean-Baptiste Loiseau-Cardin; her mother was then already dead. Probable rather than record only because the 1796 groom carries no surname.

name: Jean-Baptiste Loiseau-Cardin
notes: Father of Jeanne Loiseau. Living in February 1796, when he consented to her marriage at Sorel and signed nothing. Probable for the same reason as his daughter.

name: Jeanne Cary
notes: Jeanne Loiseau's mother, already dead in 1796. Her surname is a hard word in the register and reads most like Cary; Fary is possible. Treat the spelling as unsettled.

name: Louis Cartier
notes: Genevieve's father, a farmer at Yamaska. He married Dorothee Ritchot there on 12 January 1807, an adult son of the late Louis Cartier and Madeleine Allard, so he was born before about 1782 and his father was dead by 1807. The register gives him a dit name after Cartier that reads most like Gaguet; the reading is not certain. He was alive in February 1829, when he witnessed his daughter's marriage. A FamilySearch tree calls him Louis Joseph Napoleon Cartier, 1775 to 1858; no record read here supports the Napoleon, which would be an odd name for a child of 1775. Probable only because the whole Quebec family rests on the identification described under Genevieve.

name: Dorothée Ritchot
notes: Genevieve's mother. Her 1807 marriage names her parents as the late Michel Ritchot and Marguerite Crevier, which settles which of two Dorothee Ritchots baptised at Yamaska she was: the girl of 25 June 1784, daughter of Michel and Marguerite, and not the one of 1788, daughter of Pierre Ritchot and Josephte Robidoux. The baptism date comes from the index, not from a reading of the register.

name: Louis Cartier
notes: Father of the younger Louis, and dead by January 1807, when his son's marriage calls him the late Louis Cartier. Nothing else about him has been read yet.

name: Madeleine Allard
notes: Mother of the younger Louis Cartier, named in his 1807 marriage. The act does not mark her as dead, but this clerk's habit on that point has not been tested, so her status in 1807 is unknown.

name: Michel Ritchot
notes: Married Marguerite Crevier dit St-Francois at Saint-Francois-du-Lac on 30 January 1775, where he is written Richotte, son of the late Joseph Ritchot and Marie-Anne Giroux. He died at Yamaska on 7 November 1793 and was buried the next day, aged forty-seven, which puts his birth about 1746. The burial names no parents; FamilySearch's index attaches Joseph and Anne Giroux to it anyway, and the marriage is where those names really come from.

name: Marguerite Crevier dit St-François
notes: Married Michel Ritchot at Saint-Francois-du-Lac on 30 January 1775, daughter of the late Charles Crevier and the late Charlotte Diel, so both her parents were dead by then. Joseph Crevier St-Francois witnessed the marriage; the act does not say how he was related. She was widowed in 1793.

name: Joseph Ritchot
notes: Michel Ritchot's father, dead by January 1775. Probable only because the whole Quebec family rests on the identification described under Genevieve Cartier.

name: Marie-Anne Giroux
notes: Michel Ritchot's mother, named in his 1775 marriage. The act marks only the father as dead. Probable only because the whole Quebec family rests on the identification described under Genevieve Cartier.

name: Charles Crevier
notes: Marguerite's father, dead by January 1775. Crevier is an old Trois-Rivieres name, but no link to the early Creviers has been traced here. Probable only because the whole Quebec family rests on the identification described under Genevieve Cartier.

name: Charlotte Diel
notes: Marguerite's mother, dead by January 1775. Diel is how the register writes it. Probable only because the whole Quebec family rests on the identification described under Genevieve Cartier.

name: Joseph Bernier
notes: Lydia's father, named Joe Bernier on her death record. In the 1910 census at Centerville he is Josef, born about 1867 in French Canada, arrived 1870, with his wife and five children: John B., Lydia, Emele, Stefana and Josef Jr. Their marriage has not been found.

name: Emilie Forcier
notes: Lydia's mother, written Emmile Forcier on her daughter's death record and Emele in the 1910 census, born about 1868 in French Canada and arrived 1878. Lydia's birth index carries the Forcier name too.

name: Tellsford (Télesphore?) LaCasse
notes: Cyril's father, written Tellsford on Cyril's 1964 death record. That is almost certainly the French name Telesphore heard by an English-speaking clerk; the French form is inference.

name: Alphonsine Parenteau
notes: Cyril's mother, named on his 1964 death record.

name: John LaMotte
notes: Delina's father, named on her 1964 death record. Earlier research had the LaMotte name without a document; this is the document.

name: Rosalyn Tatreau (Tétreault?)
notes: Delina's mother, written Rosalyn Tatreau on Delina's 1964 death record. Tetreault is the likely French spelling; that is inference.
